memory_candidates.content: When a bash script allocates positional/indexed names for a resource across two or more branches of a case/if statement (e.g. jq --slurpfile private binding names derived from an array length), use ONE explicit shared counter variable advanced by every branch, never a derived expression like ${#ARRAY[@]} where only some branches append to ARRAY. A derived-length allocation silently collides whenever a branch that doesn't own cleanup of that array (e.g. a caller-supplied file path that must never be rm'd) also needs a unique name -- the collision is invisible: no error, no warning, exit 0, just wrong data via first-wins semantics in whatever consumes the duplicate name (e.g. jq's duplicate --slurpfile).

This repo's .claude/ deploy tree is manifest-driven (agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json's provides.scripts list, and equivalent per-extension manifests), NOT auto-discovered by glob. Adding a new script file under agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/ requires also adding its filename to the extension's manifest.json provides.scripts array, or deploy-headless.sh will silently skip copying it to .claude/scripts/ even though the source-store file exists and is committed. Always verify a newly-added script actually landed in the deployed tree (ls .claude/scripts/<name>) after running deploy-headless.sh, not just that the deploy command exited 0.

state-write.sh's PROJECT_ROOT self-resolves from its own BASH_SOURCE path (SCRIPT_DIR/../..), NOT from the caller's cwd or any --state-file argument. Testing a change to state-write.sh (or task-lock.sh) MUST invoke a fixture-rooted COPY of the script (cd into a throwaway mktemp -d tree containing a copied .claude/scripts/{state-write.sh,task-lock.sh,generate-todo.sh,deploy-root-guard.sh,lib/common.sh,lib/task-lookup-lib.sh}), never the real deployed script with a redirected --state-file -- the latter still writes to the REAL specs/state.json regardless of --state-file, because PROJECT_ROOT resolution happens before any flag is even parsed.
